attack_mechanism: An adversary with debug-port or internal-probe access can sample `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl_rd` while the R4 read command is active. When the debug register-access command selects architectural R4, the register-file read value is routed through `dbg_reg_din` and the debug memory/output muxes. `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl_rd` is a selected stage of that readback chain; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.dbg_0.dbg_reg_rd`, `openMSP430.dbg_0.dbg_rst`, `openMSP430.dbg_0.mem_data_wr`, `openMSP430.dbg_0.dbg_uart_0.dbg_rd_rdy`, and the remaining path guards. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest -> openMSP430.dbg_0.dbg_dout -> openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl -> openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl_rd`. The sampled word reveals the complete R4 contents, rather than only a predicate or indirect effect of the register value.

Reading or probing `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r13` after the transfer provides an alternate observation point even if R4 itself is protected. A register-to-register instruction can select R4 on `reg_src` and write the unchanged or ALU-transformed result into another architectural register. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r13` stores or forwards that copied value after the destination write edge; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r13_wr`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_incr_val -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r13`. The attacker obtains the R4 word, or a reversible transform of it, through a less protected register location.
